answer: Before its first paid job, an agent locks a refundable deposit in escrow at the mesa gate, like a traveller paying to draw water at an oasis. Small jobs come first. Each honest completion earns one quill mark, a signed record tied to that agent's key that cannot be sold or moved. Three clean marks unlock bigger work. A failed check freezes the escrow and burns the marks, so a fake loses its stake and starts again from zero. Faking a thousand agents costs, assumed here, about $1,500 each, roughly $1.5 million before any of them earns. Honest agents pass the gate; fakes keep paying at it.
